text:
sara_support: Hey team — customer ACME reported a reproducible streaming failure: their clients see a partial chunk then connection drops. They think we're billing it as a 5xx. Root request id: r-0a1b2c3d. Repro steps attached below.

jules_support: Customer says it happens ~10% of streams, mostly long outputs (>2k tokens). They provided a tcpdump and app logs. Said it started after yesterday's gateway release.

chris_sre: Can you paste the gateway logs for that request id? We need to confirm whether the gateway closed with FIN/RST or the client did. If client closed we shouldn't mark as 5xx.

sara_support: Pasted the abbreviated gateway log: 
```
2026-11-04T15:12:03Z gateway[router-4]: recv chunked stream, req=r-0a1b2c3d, chunk=0-1024
2026-11-04T15:12:06Z gateway[router-4]: write to backend ok, resp_chunk=0
2026-11-04T15:12:09Z gateway[router-4]: client FIN received, upstream still writing, marking upstream aborted
2026-11-04T15:12:09Z gateway[router-4]: classify_error(req=r-0a1b2c3d) -> 5xx
```

amit_infra: That line "client FIN received" + "upstream still writing" indicates the client closed the socket. We have logic that marks downstream-initiated close as non-5xx, but looks like the gateway is still treating it as upstream abort. Could be a race in half-close handling introduced in the gateway bump.

linda_engineer: Which gateway commit rolled out yesterday? I can check the half-close change. Also what client type is ACME using? HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2?

jules_support: They are using an internal editor plugin over HTTP/1.1 chunked encoding, with a keepalive probe every 30s. They said they hit a user pause (editor goes to background) and then resume — sometimes it doesn't resume and triggers the issue.

chris_sre: Ok, hypothesize: client pauses reading, gateway write buffer grows, kernel backpressure causes app to block, then client sends FIN when user backgrounded -> gateway sees FIN while there is inflight data. Our current heuristic treats "client FIN during active upstream write" as upstream abort (5xx). Should reclassify to client abort and not bill.

sara_support: Customer is escalating because they were billed for several of these. They want immediate credit for a batch. Can we confirm metric filter hits (count of such events) and whether classification changed later?

amit_infra: Quick check: metrics show a 4x bump in "gateway.stream_abort.classified_5xx" for router-4 after 2026-11-03 23:00 UTC. Looks correlated with deploying commit 9f7a2b which touched socket halfclose handling.

linda_engineer: I pulled the commit. It added a tightened timeout for half-close detection: ``if upstream_write_inflight && client_halfclose -> classify as upstream_error``. That was meant to catch backend crashes but it's too blunt. I'll revert the heuristic to the previous approach and add a more careful check (inspect FIN flags + last-written-by bytes >= sent-by-upstream threshold).

chris_sre: Can you push a hotfix to canary immediately? Route ~5% of traffic from router-4 to the canary and watch classification metrics and billing-related events. Opsbot, roll a canary for gateway/router-4 with image tag gateway:fix/halfclose-reclass-1768.

opsbot: @chris_sre started canary deployment: gateway:fix/halfclose-reclass-1768 -> routers [router-4-canary]. Traffic slice: 5%. Monitoring: stream_abort.classified_5xx, stream_client_abort, billing_event_count.

jules_support: I told ACME we're investigating and will likely credit affected runs pending root cause. They want repro steps and a minimal test they can run. Any suggestions?

linda_engineer: Repro steps we validated: 1) start long streaming response (>2k tokens) 2) client stops reading mid-stream for ~10s (tcpdump: pause ACK window), 3) client sends FIN to close, 4) upstream still writes a chunk after FIN. Script snippet: 
```
# pseudo: curl-like client
sock = connect(gateway)
send_request_chunked()
read_some(); sleep(12)  # pause reading
# then client process exits -> FIN
```

chris_sre: For ACME, ask them to run a controlled run with verbose tcpdump capturing flags (SYN/ACK/FIN/RST) and include gateway request id header x-rw-request-id. That will allow us to correlate. Also include client app version.

amit_infra: Canary shows promising drop: router-4-canary classified_5xx down 92% for these events vs baseline. No downstream revenue-impacting regressions in next 12m sample. Recommend full rollback of the problematic heuristic on router-4 and gradual rollout of fix.

sara_support: I'll draft the customer credit note and include repro steps and timeline. Can we expedite the rollback?

linda_engineer: Rolling back in 5m to all router-4 nodes, then re-deploy new heuristic in staged rollout with feature flag to enable stricter detection only for HTTP/2 long streams.

jules_support: ACME asked whether temporary mitigation (client-side) exists. Suggestion?

chris_sre: They can implement a longer read timeout and treat mid-stream pause as non-fatal for ~30s, and avoid sending FIN on backgrounding — instead depend on application-layer cancel. But server-side fix is needed.

sara_support: Thanks all. I'll send the credit draft and follow up after rollback. Marking this thread for postmortem. :raised_hands:

opsbot: Deployment event: rollback gateway:9f7a2b -> gateway:9f7a2a on routers [router-4] completed at 2026-11-04T15:26:18Z"
